adulis-houston.our_story: Adulis brings Eritrean and Ethiopian hospitality to Bellaire Boulevard—a family-owned room where injera platters, tibs, and coffee ceremonies keep Houston's Habesha community fed late into the night.
adulis-houston.cultural_roots: Horn of Africa table culture: communal injera, berbere spice, and the shared-plate rituals that tie Eritrean and Ethiopian kitchens together.

lucilles-houston.our_story: Chef Chris Williams named Lucille's for his great-grandmother, turning a Museum District bungalow into one of Houston's most celebrated Southern fine-dining rooms—chili biscuits, yardbird, and history on every plate.
lucilles-houston.cultural_roots: Texas Southern cooking with Black American heritage at its center: comfort food elevated through technique, family memory, and Gulf Coast ingredients.

cool-runnings-jamaican-grill-houston.our_story: Cool Runnings Jamaican Grill earned national attention on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives while staying a neighborhood favorite—brown stew snapper, escovitch fish, and patty-shop warmth without the pretense.

fabaceae-african-cuisine-houston.cultural_roots: Nigerian chop-house traditions: swallow and soup pairings, slow-stewed meats, and the bold seasoning of Lagos and southwestern Nigeria.

sarabell-calabar-houston.our_story: Sarabell Calabar specializes in the seafood-rich cooking of Nigeria's Cross River region—edikang ikong, afang soup, and Calabar stews served with the depth of flavor the cuisine is known for.
sarabell-calabar-houston.cultural_roots: Calabar culinary heritage: leafy greens, smoked fish, palm oil, and the coastal Nigerian stews built around fresh catch and forest herbs.

africa-kine-new-york.our_story: Africa Kine has anchored Little Senegal in Harlem since 1994—lamb mafe, chicken yassa, and grilled fish in a halal dining room that feels like stepping into Dakar.
africa-kine-new-york.cultural_roots: Senegalese home cooking: peanut-stew mafe, citrus-marinated yassa, and thieboudienne traditions from West Africa's Atlantic coast.
